title: UK Stamp Duty Update Starting April 2025 - Silver Oak Capital
summary: Blog article (not a case study). Thesis per the search tool's summary [b]: a forward-looking piece, written before 1 April 2025, explaining the upcoming Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) changes in the UK. It describes SDLT as a tax levied on property purchases in England and Northern Ireland that applies to residential, buy-to-let and commercial property transactions. Concrete guidance it gives: the temporary SDLT relief was expected to end in April 2025; the standard residential nil-rate threshold would revert to £125,000 from £250,000; the first-time buyer relief cap would fall from £425,000 to £300,000; and the additional-property surcharge was described as 'currently an additional 3% surcharge' with speculation of a rise to '4% or higher'. The search tool flagged that this surcharge figure is outdated: the Finance Act 2025 raised the additional-dwellings rate for transactions from 31 October 2024 (5% on the first £250,000). No H1, meta description, section headings, FAQ, process steps or calls to action were revealed by the results.

Standard residential nil-rate threshold reverting to £125,000 from £250,000
First-time buyer relief cap reduced from £425,000 to £300,000

eligibility: Standard residential purchases: nil-rate threshold reverts to £125,000 (from £250,000) from April 2025 (per the article, as summarised in [b])
First-time buyers: relief cap reduced from £425,000 to £300,000 from April 2025 (per the article, as summarised in [b])
Additional-property purchasers (buy-to-let / second homes): pay a surcharge on top of standard rates; article cites 3% at time of writing (outdated)
Scope: SDLT applies in England and Northern Ireland only (Scotland and Wales have separate regimes - stated by the search tool, not by the article)
